chunks: We said: Protection (al-Mana') is of two kinds: one is not incompatible with religious duty, as it does not compel the subject to forsake the wrong; and the other leads to such compulsion.

The first kind Allah has enacted, by preventing oppression against him through forbidding it, encouraging the obligation of obedience to him, compliance with his command and prohibition, that he not be disobeyed in any of his commands, and that he be helped in all that strengthens his authority and consolidates his power. Indeed, all of this is not incompatible with duty. So if someone disobeys in this regard and does not do what is required for the desired objective to be realized, he has acted on his own, not from his Creator.

The other kind is that He literally separates them from him by force and renders them incapable of oppressing and disobeying him. Therefore, this is not compatible with religious duty, which requires free choice, and thus, religious obligations must be annulled.

key_terms.التَّكْلِيلَ: Religious duty or conferment of obligations

ai.seo_question: How does divine protection of the Imam differ between preserving free will and removing it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi elucidates the theological nuance of divine prevention (al-Mana') during the Occultation, distinguishing between prohibitive commands that preserve human agency and coercive force that would nullify religious duty. This distinction safeguards the concept of *taklif* (obligation) by ensuring that the Imam’s absence does not equate to divine abandonment or irresistible compulsion. It underscores the Shia view that the Imam’s guidance remains effective through spiritual and legal frameworks rather than physical intervention.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: We would reply: Protection is of two kinds. One is not incompatible with conferment of religious duties as it does not compel the subject to forsake the wrong. The other kind of protection leads to such compulsion.

And Allah has provided the first protection, as He has protected the Imam from oppression by forbidding it and by encouraging obedience to him and compliance to his orders and prohibitions and that he may not be disobeyed in any of his orders and that he should be helped in all matters that strengthen his rule and power. All such measures are compatible with conferment of obligations. If someone disobeys with this regard and does not take necessary measures for this objective to materialize, he has done that on his own, and it is not the act of his Creator.

The other kind of protection is that He literally protects him from his enemies by force and compulsion and by rendering them incapable of oppressing and disobeying him. Therefore, this is not compatible with religious duties, which require free choice in order to have meaning, and thus, religious obligations must be annulled.
